title: Police Station
statementMd:
The Berland road network consists of $*n*$ cities and of $*m*$ bidirectional roads. The cities are numbered from 1 to $*n*$, where the main capital city has number $*n*$, and the culture capital — number $1$. The road network is set up so that it is possible to reach any city from any other one by the roads. Moving on each road in any direction takes the same time.

All residents of Berland are very lazy people, and so when they want to get from city $*v*$ to city $*u*$, they always choose one of the shortest paths (no matter which one).

The Berland government wants to make this country's road network safer. For that, it is going to put a police station in one city. The police station has a rather strange property: when a citizen of Berland is driving along the road with a police station at one end of it, the citizen drives more carefully, so all such roads are considered safe. The roads, both ends of which differ from the city with the police station, are dangerous.

Now the government wonders where to put the police station so that the average number of safe roads for **all** the shortest paths from the cultural capital to the main capital would take the maximum value.

## Input

The first input line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/830edae867a954b8b9fed8adb7a01c55020312a0.png)) — the number of cities and the number of roads in Berland, correspondingly. Next $*m*$ lines contain pairs of integers $*v*_{*i*}$, $*u*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *v*_{*i*}, *u*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $*v*_{*i*} ≠ *u*_{*i*}$) — the numbers of cities that are connected by the $*i*$-th road. The numbers on a line are separated by a space.

It is guaranteed that each pair of cities is connected with no more than one road and that it is possible to get from any city to any other one along Berland roads.

## Output

Print the maximum possible value of the average number of safe roads among all shortest paths from the culture capital to the main one. The answer will be considered valid if its absolute or relative inaccuracy does not exceed $10^{ - 6}$.

## Note

In the first sample you can put a police station in one of the capitals, then each path will have exactly one safe road. If we place the station not in the capital, then the average number of safe roads will also make ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8f23cc2cd3bef67bde56e16911c7af627da25d4d.png).

In the second sample we can obtain the maximum sought value if we put the station in city $4$, then $6$ paths will have $2$ safe roads each, and one path will have $0$ safe roads, so the answer will equal ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d7723df54e28c93b1c3b9d4c68b039b5071092af.png).
statementZhMd:
伯兰德的道路网络由 $*n*$ 个城市和 $*m*$ 条双向道路组成。城市编号从 1 到 $*n*$，其中首都的编号为 $*n*$，文化首都的编号为 $1$。道路网络保证可以通过道路从任意城市到达其他任意城市。沿每条道路向任意方向行驶所需的时间相同。

所有伯兰德居民都非常懒惰，因此当他们想要从城市 $*v*$ 前往城市 $*u*$ 时，总会选择一条最短路径（至于选择哪一条并不重要）。

伯兰德政府希望让这个国家的道路网络更加安全。为此，他们打算在某个城市建造一座警察局。警察局具有一个相当奇特的性质：当伯兰德居民沿着一端设有警察局的道路行驶时，会更加小心，因此所有这样的道路都被视为安全道路。两端都不与警察局所在城市相连的道路则是危险道路。

现在，政府想知道应当将警察局建在哪个城市，才能使从文化首都到首都的所有最短路径中，安全道路数量的平均值最大。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/830edae867a954b8b9fed8adb7a01c55020312a0.png)），分别表示伯兰德的城市数和道路数。接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*v*_{*i*}$、$*u*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *v*_{*i*}, *u*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*v*_{*i*} ≠ *u*_{*i*}$），表示第 $*i*$ 条道路连接的两个城市。每行中的数字由空格分隔。

保证任意一对城市之间至多有一条道路，并且可以沿着伯兰德的道路从任意城市到达其他任意城市。

## 输出格式

输出从文化首都到首都的所有最短路径中，安全道路数量平均值的最大可能值。如果答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 6}$，则会被视为正确。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，可以将警察局建在两个首都中的任意一个城市，此时每条路径恰好有一条安全道路。如果将警察局建在非首都城市，安全道路数量的平均值也会达到![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8f23cc2cd3bef67bde56e16911c7af627da25d4d.png)。

在第二个样例中，将警察局建在城市 $4$ 可以得到所求的最大值。此时有 $6$ 条路径各自包含 $2$ 条安全道路，另有一条路径包含 $0$ 条安全道路，因此答案为![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d7723df54e28c93b1c3b9d4c68b039b5071092af.png)。
